modern:
How can it be that the gods, after arranging all things well and kindly for mankind, have overlooked this alone: that some men, and very good men, men who, as we may say, have had the closest communion with the divine, and through pious acts and religious observances have been most intimate with the divine, should never exist again once they have died, but should be completely extinguished?

But if this is so, be assured that if it ought to have been otherwise, the gods would have done it. For if it were just, it would also be possible; and if it were according to nature, nature would have had it so. But because it is not so, if in fact it is not so, be convinced that it ought not to have been so: for you see even for yourself that in this inquiry you are arguing with the Deity; and we would not argue like this with the gods unless they were most excellent and most just; but if this is so, they would not have allowed anything in the ordering of the universe to be neglected unjustly and irrationally.
original:
How can it be that the gods, after having arranged all things well and benevolently for mankind, have overlooked this alone, that some men, and very good men, and men who, as we may say, have had most communion with the divinity, and through pious acts and religious observances have been most intimate with the divinity, when they have once died should never exist again, but should be completely extinguished?

But if this is so, be assured that if it ought to have been otherwise, the gods would have done it. For if it were just, it would also be possible; and if it were according to nature, nature would have had it so. But because it is not so, if in fact it is not so, be thou convinced that it ought not to have been so: for thou seest even of thyself that in this inquiry thou art disputing with the Deity; and we should not thus dispute with the gods, unless they were most excellent and most just; but if this is so, they would not have allowed anything in the ordering of the universe to be neglected unjustly and irrationally.

explained.summary:
Marcus raises a hard question: if the gods arranged everything so well for humans, why let the very best people, those closest to the divine, simply vanish for good at death? He doesn’t pretend to have an answer.

Instead he reasons that if it would have been right for them to survive, the gods would have made it so, because what is just is also possible for them. The fact that he can even put this complaint to the gods assumes they are good and fair, and good and fair gods wouldn’t leave something unjust in the universe. So, if this is how things are, it must be how they ought to be.
